title: Adaptive throttle rollback and token race retrospective
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Summary: On 2025-02-11 we observed a multi-region 429 surge that affected hosted API customers for ~28 minutes. The visible symptom was a sudden spike in 429 responses from the edge API gateway, disproportionately affecting long-lived chat sessions. Impact included elevated latency, failed client retries, and multiple support tickets from high-usage customers. This ticket captures the investigation, primary root causes, temporary mitigations, and tracked action items for long-term fixes.

What happened (short): A canary deployment of a new adaptive throttling policy increased enforcement sensitivity in some edge nodes while an unrelated auth token-caching regression caused token-mismatch checks to skip shared quota lookups. The combination made a subset of requests appear to exceed quota and triggered cascading global throttles and aggressive backoff behavior in the gateway.

Why this is unique: Previous 429 incidents were typically quota-misconfiguration or quota-sync delay issues. This incident was a compound failure where a rollout changed enforcement thresholds and an auth cache race created false negatives for quota coordination, producing a 429 amplification effect across routing tiers.
investigation_notes: 02-11 08:41 UTC - First alert: sudden 4x increase in 429 rate from edge-eu-1. Paging triggered.
Traffic pattern: spike concentrated on chat endpoints with long-lived streaming sessions; token refresh paths showed anomalous traffic bursts.
Configuration rollouts: adaptive-throttle v3.1 deployed via progressive canary between 08:30-08:38 UTC across regions.

Auth service change: short-lived token cache refactor (auth-cache v2.4) deployed at 07:50 UTC; introduced a subtle race where stale token metadata could be read during concurrent validate/refresh flows.
Correlation: nodes that received both the throttle change and the auth-cache refactor exhibited ~3.5x higher 429s than nodes with only one of the changes.
Logs: quota-lookup failures logged as transient 'quota_key_not_found' with 200ms higher median latency on affected nodes; these failures caused throttling fallback to aggressive per-token limits.

Immediate rollback: rollbacks initiated - adaptive-throttle rolled back to v3.0 at 08:55 UTC; auth-cache hotfix deployed to revert refactor at 09:10 UTC. 429 rates returned to baseline by 09:05-09:20 UTC depending on region.

Root causes: (1) adaptive-throttle sensitivity change reduced headroom for bursts; (2) auth-cache race allowed stale token state that prevented correct quota attribution; (3) insufficient canary granularity - canary overlap allowed both changes to land on same subset of nodes simultaneously.
Observability gaps: quota attribution logs lacked request-level token->quota mapping; rollout dashboards did not highlight overlapping change windows across dependent subsystems.
Customer impact assessment: major enterprise customers saw degraded throughput and increased error rates for streaming chat. No data exfiltration or unauthorized access observed.
Related incidents: links to token-race investigations (ENG-19987) and quota-enforcer cache consistency work (ENG-17521).
action_items: A1: Add strict pre-deploy gating that prevents simultaneous canary window for throttling and auth-service changes. Owner: Jonas Kim. Due: 2025-02-28.
A2: Implement request-level quota attribution logs (sampled) to trace token->quota decisions; retention for 14 days. Owner: Elena Sanchez. Estimate: 3. Due: 2025-03-12.
A3: Harden auth token cache: add CAS-style validation during refresh paths to eliminate stale-read race. Owner: Priya Rao. Estimate: 5. Due: 2025-03-05.

A4: Add a canary overlap detector in deployment pipeline that blocks overlapping canaries if subsystems have cross-dependencies. Owner: Platform CI team (lead: Omar Feld). Estimate: 2. Due: 2025-03-01.
A5: Create automated throttling rollback playbook and add a runbook step to identify 'false quota' signatures. Owner: SRE (lead: Nikhil Verma). Due: 2025-03-03.
A6: Run a targeted capacity test exercising long-lived streaming sessions with token refresh churn to validate new throttle settings before rollout. Owner: Reliability QA. Due: 2025-03-10.
A7: Notify top 20 customers of incident summary, remediation, and upcoming mitigations; prepare a compensation proposal if requested. Owner: Customer Success (lead: Hannah Le). Due: 2025-02-21.
A8: Add a monitoring alert for 'quota attribution failure' rate crossing 0.5% to proactively page. Owner: Observability team. Due: 2025-02-24.
A9: Postmortem write-up review with legal/security to confirm no exposure; archive artifacts and link to ticket. Owner: Security (lead: Omar Shah). Due: 2025-02-22.
A10: Update rollout checklist to require explicit dependency review for throttle/auth changes. Owner: Product Operations. Due: 2025-02-27.
